Renal ultrasound shows bilaterally enlarged kidneys containing multiple parenchymal anechoic masses — classic appearance of multiple renal cysts. The combination of bilateral, symmetric renal cysts with enlarged, palpable kidneys, hypertension, recurrent UTIs, and declining renal function in a 31-year-old is most consistent with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Other cystic disorders (medullary sponge kidney, simple cysts, acquired cystic disease) are less likely given the bilateral enlargement, number of cysts, age, and clinical features. Family history is not provided but a de novo mutation can occur.  
DIAGNOSIS: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD)
